beats.text: Why does sad music feel so good?
In a survey of over seven hundred people, researchers asked how sad music makes them feel.
The most common answer wasn't sadness. It was nostalgia. Then peacefulness, and tenderness.
And people reached for it most when they felt lonely or down.
So sad songs aren't making it worse. They're keeping you company.

sources: Taruffi & Koelsch (2014). The paradox of music-evoked sadness: An online survey. PLOS ONE 9(10). 772 participants; nostalgia most frequent, also peacefulness, tenderness, transcendence, wonder; listened to when emotionally distressed or lonely. Via Pacific Standard.
